instructions: Toast the bread until it's lightly golden and dry. Cut each slice into 4 squares.

Cut the roots off 2 stems of cilantro and chop them finely with the garlic. Mash them together with the side of your knife into a rough paste, then stir in the white pepper. Pick 24 cilantro leaves and set them aside.
In a bowl, mix the pork with the soy sauce, the pinch of sugar and the garlic paste, using your hand until it's evenly combined.
Beat the egg and mix it into the pork until it's smooth and sticky.
Spread about 1 tsp of the pork over each bread square, right to the edges. Press a cilantro leaf on top of each.
Heat the oil in a wide, deep skillet over medium-high heat until a small bit of pork sizzles right away when you drop it in.
Stand back a little. They'll spatter. Slide in 6 to 8 toasts, pork side down, and fry for 1 minute, until the pork side is golden.
Flip them and fry the other side for 30 seconds. Transfer them to a plate lined with paper towels.
Repeat with the remaining toasts. You're cooking the pork to 160°F, so if you have a thermometer, check one there. No thermometer? Break one open: it's done when there's no pink left.
Serve with the sweet chili sauce.
method_notes: Cooking with Nart leads (5 from 11 votes, under 20, so this is a fallback lead): toasted bread, a pounded cilantro root, white pepper and garlic paste, and a pork mix bound with one egg. Rachel Cooks Thai and Don't Go Bacon My Heart agree on the same paste and a quick fry pork side down; they also dip the bread in egg, which this version skips. The sources serve a cucumber relish; this one uses a bottled sweet chili sauce instead. Written for 24 pieces (6 per person); it takes about 40 minutes, over the list's 15.
